paper.title: The Sample Complexity of Uniform Approximation for Multi-Dimensional CDFs and Fixed-Price Mechanisms

settings.name_in_paper: Learning a uniform approximation of an n-dimensional CDF over a uniform grid G_K with one-bit feedback
unmapped: Query points x_t in [0,1]^n; feedback is the bit I[X_t <= x_t] for a fresh sample X_t ~ D (arbitrary distribution on [0,1]^n)
Goal: output estimate P~ with sup error <= epsilon over a uniform grid G_K of resolution 1/K (K known to learner), w.p. >= 1-delta
Target is a monotone CDF structure (no vocabulary term)
settings.definition_quote: At each round t, an independent sample X_t ~ D is drawn, we select a query point x_t in [0,1]^n, and we observe the single bit I[X_t <= x_t] ... We relax the requirement ... so that it holds only over a finite uniform grid.

settings.name_in_paper: Uniform approximation of an n-dimensional CDF with bounded density (whole domain)
unmapped: Distribution D has a density bounded by sigma (known to the learner, used to set the grid)
Goal: uniform epsilon-approximation of the CDF over all of [0,1]^n w.p. >= 1-delta
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the probability distribution D has bounded density, which means that it admits a probability density function d: [0,1]^n -> R that is upper bounded by some constant sigma > 0 everywhere.

settings.name_in_paper: Sample complexity of learning an approximately optimal fixed-price mechanism in small markets
unmapped: Objective E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) with known L-Lipschitz (l1) utility f: [0,1]^n -> [0,1]; trade probability is a CDF after affine transform
Feedback is only the binary trade outcome Trade(V_t,p_t)
n = n_s + n_b agents (sellers and buyers); joint valuation distribution arbitrary
settings.definition_quote: given an error epsilon > 0 and a confidence delta in (0,1), the goal is to find a p* in [0,1]^n such that, with probability at least 1-delta: E[Trade(V,p*)] f(p*) >= max_p E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) - epsilon.

settings.name_in_paper: Regret minimization for fixed-price mechanisms in small markets
unmapped: Reward E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) with known L-Lipschitz utility f; only binary trade outcome observed
settings.definition_quote: REG_T := T max_p E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) - sum_t E[Trade(V,p_t)] f(p_t).

RHI + CGE on a grid with K = 2 sigma n / epsilon (bounded density extension)

symbols.c_exp: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

tuning: internal accuracy epsilon' = epsilon / (2^{n+3} sqrt(n ln(4K/delta)) (log2 K)^n)

source.label: theo: main
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, given an accuracy $\epsilon > 0$, a confidence $\delta \in (0,1)$, and a uniform grid $\mathcal{G}_K$ over $[0,1]^n$ of resolution $1 / K$ (with $K \in \mathbb{N}$), uses $\frac{1}{\epsilon^3}\log(K/\delta)^{\mathcal{O}(n)}$ queries and outputs a function $\widetilde P: \mathcal{G}_K \to [0,1]$ such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, ... $\le \epsilon \quad \forall x \in \mathcal{G}_K$.

results.notes: Guarantee: sup over grid of |CDF - P~| <= epsilon w.p. 1-delta. Proof gives n^2 log2(K/delta)^{O(n)}/eps^3. Corollary 6.1 restates this for trade probabilities in small markets (same expression).

symbols.sigma_dens: upper bound on the probability density of D
symbols.c_exp: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

conditions: D admits a density bounded by sigma

source.label: theo: mainSmooth
source.quote: Assume that the distribution $\cD$ admits density bounded by $\sigma > 0$. Then, there exists an algorithm that, given an accuracy $\epsilon > 0$ and a confidence $\delta \in (0,1)$, uses $\frac{1}{\epsilon^3}\log(\sigma n/(\epsilon\delta))^{\mathcal{O}(n)}$ samples and outputs a function $\widetilde P : [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$ such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$: ... $\forall x \in [0,1]^n$.

results.notes: Uniform approximation over the whole domain.

symbols.c_exp: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent
symbols.d: number of agents n = n_s + n_b

conditions: f: [0,1]^n -> [0,1] is known and L-Lipschitz w.r.t. l1 norm

source.label: thm:pricing
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, given an accuracy $\epsilon>0$, a confidence $\delta \in (0,1)$, and a $L$-Lipschitz function $f: [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$, uses $\log(nL/(\delta\epsilon))^{\mathcal{O}(n)}\frac{1}{\epsilon^3}$ queries and outputs a solution $p^\star \in [0,1]^n$ such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, ... $\geq \max_{p} ... - \epsilon$.

results.notes: Returns an epsilon-optimal fixed-price mechanism w.p. 1-delta.

symbols.c_exp: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

source.label: theo: mainFixedPriceRegret
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, given a number of rounds $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and a $L$-Lipschitz function $f: [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$, achieves regret: $\textsf{REG}_T \coloneqq T \cdot \max_{p} \mathbb{E}[\Trade(V,p)] f(p) - \sum_{t\in [T]} \mathbb{E}[\Trade(V,p_t)] f(p_t) \le \log(nLT)^{\mathcal{O}(n)} T^{3/4}.$

results.notes: Regret defined via expected per-round utilities with random p_t but no outer expectation; proof bounds it on a probability 1-1/T event and says the statement follows. Recorded as regret_unspecified; probability field set to expectation as the closest fit, uncertain.
